title: Resolution model for normalized global site comparison
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Use small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-size-convention], with their constant-$\Lambda$ module categories and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes, $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison inverse image, and $N_T=\nu_{T,*}$ for its right adjoint [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].
Let $U$ be a scheme and $F$ a $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. There exist nonnegative complexes $I,J$, termwise injective and K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and quasi-isomorphisms $i:F[0]\to I$ and $t:A_UI\to J$. For every such pair, $t\circ A_U(i)$ identifies $QJ$ canonically with $A_UF[0]$.
Let $h:I\to N_UJ$ be the chain map adjoint to $t$ and let $w:\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},I)\to\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proet}},J)$ be its evaluation at the final object, using $(N_UJ)(U)=J(U)$. Under the canonical resolution identifications for derived sections, $Qw$ is the global comparison induced by the derived comparison unit and the final-object isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology, lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward]. Thus, for every $q\geq0$ and global degree-$q$ cocycle $z$ of $I$, the specified map $c^q_{U,F}$ sends the global class of $z$ to the global class of $h(z)$ in $J$. Moreover $h(z)=t(A_U(z))$, where $A_U(z)$ means comparison pullback of the terminal section, using the canonical constant-ring unit identification. This holds without requiring $A_U$ to preserve injective objects.

source.place: Opening paragraph, transport of classes from the etale site to the pro-etale site. Agent-stated resolution refinement; supporting interfaces: Stacks Tag 099W, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-cohomology; Stacks Tag 079P, injectives.tex, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck. Neither tag verbatim states this normalized chain model.

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck-abelian instances for ModuleCat-valued sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites and the enough-injectives instance. Resolve F[0] by the lower-bound-preserving injective-resolution lemma at bound zero, obtaining i:F[0] to I with injective terms and zero negative terms. The additive comparison pullback preserves zero objects, so A(I) is nonnegative. Apply the same lemma again to obtain t:A(I) to J, with J nonnegative and termwise injective. The bounded-below injectivity theorem makes both complexes K-injective. Package the actual complexes and maps; no resolution data is selected from an unproved arbitrary existence statement in a definition.

source.place: Tag 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), part (3), with a=0; Tag 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective). Enough injectives: injectives.tex Tags 079Q (remark-existence-D) and 079H (theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck). Existing fixed-ring sheaf instances: WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckAbelian/Sheaf.lean, isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_smallEtaleTopology and isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_proEtTopology.

proof.text: Now take any pair $i,t$ allowed in the statement, not only those just constructed. Put $\rho=Qi$ and $\beta=Q(t\circ A_U(i))$. Exact comparison pullback carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so $\rho$, $Q(A_U(i))$, $Qt$, and $\beta$ are isomorphisms. In the termwise exact-pullback identification, $\beta=(Qt)\circ A_U(\rho):A_UF[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$. This is the specified identification of the target; its inverse identifies $QJ$ with $A_UF[0]$.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), followed by the definition of localization and composition.

proof.text: Let $\eta^0$ be the ordinary comparison unit, applied termwise. The comparison-morphism node supplies the additive adjunction $A_U\dashv N_U$, so the termwise-adjunction theorem gives the chain map $h=N_U(t)\circ\eta^0_I:I\to N_UJ$, its adjoint being $t$. The direct image is restriction along the inclusion of etale objects. In particular $(N_UJ^n)(U)=J^n(U)$, with the same coefficient action and differential. Thus evaluation of $h$ is exactly the specified chain map $w:\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}I\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{proet}}J$.

source.place: Tag 099R (section-comparison), inclusion sending U/X to U/X; termwise adjunction is the additive adjunction on complexes, as in derived.tex Tag 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors).

proof.text: Let G and Gprime denote the two terminal evaluation functors, rho=Qi, beta the target identification, alphaI and alphaJ their actual right-derived units at I and J. The units are invertible on these termwise injective complexes. Define eI=alphaI followed by the inverse of RG(rho), and eJ=alphaJ followed by the inverse of RGprime(beta). Cancellation immediately gives the two required normalizations. Only the injectivity of I and J is needed; no injectivity assertion about the direct image of J is used.

source.place: Tag 070Y, computation on bounded-below injective complexes; Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/DerivabilityStructureInjectives.lean, invertibility of the right-derived unit on injective terms.

proof.text: Use the recorded definition of finiteComparisonGlobalSections as rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange of the terminal evaluation of the ordinary comparison unit. Evaluate its defining unit compatibility at I. Naturality of the identity-derived isomorphism removes the derived identity, and its localization-factor equation cancels the extra identity factor. Postcompose with RGprime of the exact-pullback factor followed by Qt. The inverse and forward localization factors cancel. Naturality of alpha at t then identifies the result as Qw followed by alphaJ, because the termwise adjoint is N(t) composed with the unit, evaluated at the terminal object. This is a direct proof from the specified global comparison, without transporting through the coefficient-category encoding or the separate derived-unit model.

source.place: Tags 099R and 099W. Formal unit compatibility: WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/RightDerivedFunctor/PlusBaseChange.lean, rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac. Identity factor: WeilConjectures/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.lean, mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso_hom_app_factorsh. The global map is exactly the existing finiteComparisonGlobalSections definition.

proof.text: Naturality of the exact-pullback localization factor at i expresses beta as A(rho), then the factor at I, then Qt. Naturality of the normalized global-comparison natural transformation at rho gives its transport to F[0]. Cancel RGprime(beta), use the preceding computation and the definitions of eI and eJ, and cancel RG(rho). The resulting equality is Qw followed by eJ equals eI followed by the specified global comparison. Both computing identifications are pinned to the supplied augmentations, and the calculation applies to every pair.

source.place: Tag 099W, with derived-unit compatibility from the preceding step; the remaining argument is naturality and cancellation of isomorphisms.

proof.text: The naturality of the homology-factor isomorphisms and of homology projection proves that the localized homology map of any chain map carries the defined cycle class to the class of its cyclesMap image. Apply homology to the comparison equality from the preceding step and evaluate it on the cycle class of z. This gives the stated cocycle formula, including q=0. The last displayed equality is definitional: the hom-equivalence sends t to the comparison unit followed by N(t), and restriction evaluates at the same terminal object. No preservation of injectives by A is required.

source.place: Tag 099R (section-comparison), with the explicit adjunction-unit formula in def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact) for the canonical coefficient identification. The cycle and boundary calculation is elementary.

tool_uses.why: Generic Grothendieck property of module sheaves on either small site, needed to obtain enough injectives.
Generic resolution existence retaining a=0; this preserves the required nonnegative bound.
The fixed finite-coefficient comparison inverse image is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
Generic passage of an additive adjunction to chain maps, fixing h as the actual adjunct of t.
The specified final-object comparison, which identifies the evaluated representative with the pro-etale section complex.
The fixed definition of global comparison as derived unit followed by final-object comparison.
